title: Exploring the Fremont Bridge bike counts
intro:
A grounded EDA narrative built from a declarative spec. Each beat is a question; the builder renders the vetted hvPlot/HoloViews code. No Panel until the data outgrows the notebook.

**Question:** does this data have a daily rhythm, does it differ by day and direction, and is the uptick real?
setup:
from sample_data import sample_fremont
df = sample_fremont()   # swap for: pd.read_csv('FremontHourly.csv', parse_dates=['Date'], index_col='Date')
df.head()

beats.narrate:
## 0. What are we holding?

Profile first. The plan flags `East`/`West`/`Total` as measures and `Date` as temporal — that is what seeds every section below.

params.title: Weekly ridership — trend, seasonality, weather wobble

beats.narrate:
## 1. Zoom out — the raw signal is noise

Hourly is hash. Weekly totals expose a ~2x summer/winter swing and a slow multi-year climb: some uptick is real, but a lot of any short window is just weather.

params.title: The daily rhythm: two commute peaks

beats.narrate:
## 2. The daily rhythm

Average over hour-of-day: sharp peaks at ~8am and ~5pm, a midday lull, near-zero overnight. This is a commuter counter.

## 3. Whose rhythm? Weekday vs weekend

Condition on one more dimension and the single rhythm splits in two: weekdays bimodal (commute), weekends a single midday hump. One average hid two populations.

params.title: Mean riders by hour x weekday (the weekly fingerprint)

beats.narrate:
## 4. The whole week at a glance

Both conditioning dimensions on one panel. The commute ridge glows Mon-Fri at 8 and 17; the weekend is a soft midday smear.

params.title: Each day as a point - PCA of daily shape

beats.narrate:
## 5. Let the data name its own categories

Treat each day as a 24-D shape vector, reduce with an SVD. PC1 alone separates commute-shaped from leisure-shaped days, unsupervised — and the weekdays that land with weekends are the holidays.
